slots.practicalActivity: Read the full Lesson 1 Definition-of-Done checklist and the Lesson 2 scenario for Cascade Foodservice Equipment Co. (industry, departments, the five Opportunity stages, the four lead sources, and the seven named people). Start a document called "Capstone Requirements Checklist" with the 10-row Definition-of-Done table (leave a blank "Built in Lesson ___" column), then add a "Scenario Reference" page copying in the company name, the five stage names, and the seven-person table exactly as given.
slots.deliverable: A started capstone document containing the 10-row Definition of Done checklist and a Scenario Reference page with Cascade's stages, lead sources, and people table.

slots.practicalActivity: Draw Cascade's full object-relationship diagram by hand or in any diagramming tool, using the lesson's ASCII diagram as your starting point: Lead converting into Account/Contact/Opportunity, Opportunity carrying Opportunity Products tied to Products, a won Opportunity producing an Installation Project, and Service Contract referencing both Account and Installation Project. Label every relationship Lookup or Master-Detail, and write one sentence per custom object justifying why it's custom instead of standard.
slots.deliverable: A hand-drawn or diagrammed Cascade object-relationship diagram with every relationship labeled Lookup/Master-Detail and a one-sentence justification for each custom object.

slots.practicalActivity: Draw Cascade's seven-role hierarchy tree (VP of Sales at the top, with Priya Nair, Angela Wu, and Marcus Webb as separate branches reporting directly to her instead of through the Sales Manager). Write out the five-profile table and the five-object Organization-Wide Defaults table from the lesson, then write one sentence per sharing rule (Service to Opportunity, Customer Success to Opportunity, Key Accounts to Installation Project) explaining exactly which visibility gap each one closes.
slots.deliverable: A written security-design packet: the role-hierarchy tree, the profile and OWD tables, and three sentences explaining each sharing rule's purpose.

slots.practicalActivity: Copy the lesson's 11-row build-sequence table into your capstone document as a literal checklist, placed directly under the Lesson 1 Definition of Done. Annotate each row with the specific dependency that forces it into that position — for example, why the custom objects in row 4 must exist before the sharing rules built in row 6 can reference them.
slots.deliverable: An 11-row build-sequence checklist added to the capstone document, with each row annotated with its real dependency on an earlier row.

slots.practicalActivity: Before touching Setup in Chapter 2, assemble the three Chapter 1 artifacts into one finished design packet: the data model diagram, the security model (role hierarchy, profiles, OWD, sharing rules), and the build sequence. Review all three side by side and resolve any inconsistency between them now, on paper — Chapter 2 assumes every one of these decisions is already settled and will not revisit them.
slots.deliverable: A single finished "Cascade Design Packet" document combining the data model diagram, the security model, and the build sequence, with no open inconsistencies between them.

slots.practicalActivity: In your own Developer Edition org, create all six Account Record Types (Restaurant, Hotel & Hospitality, Healthcare & Institutional, Education, Catering, Dealer) and all six custom fields — three on Account (Business Segment, Number of Kitchen Locations, Primary Equipment Interest) and three on Contact (Contact Role, Decision Maker, Preferred Contact Method) — setting field-level security per profile exactly as specified. Create one test Account of each Record Type with Business Segment set to match.
slots.deliverable: A Developer Edition org with six configured Account Record Types, six custom fields with field-level security set, and six test Accounts, one per Record Type.

slots.practicalActivity: Replace the Lead Source picklist's default values with Cascade's four (Trade Show, Website Inquiry, Referral, Partner/Dealer), create the three Lead custom fields, and build the full lead-conversion field mapping to Account, Contact, and Opportunity exactly as specified. Create a test Lead (Lead Source = Trade Show, Trade Show Name filled in, Interested Equipment Category set, Estimated Locations = 12), convert it, and verify Primary Equipment Interest and Number of Kitchen Locations populate correctly on the new Account and that a new Opportunity exists in the Qualifying stage.
slots.deliverable: A working Lead-to-Account/Contact/Opportunity conversion mapping, verified by converting one test Lead and confirming every mapped field landed correctly.

slots.practicalActivity: Replace the Opportunity Stage picklist with Cascade's five named stages and their probabilities/forecast categories, add the Loss Reason, Target Install Quarter, and Competing Vendor fields, and build the four-product Price Book. Create one test Opportunity in each stage, attach at least one product to each, and confirm Probability and Forecast Category auto-populate correctly from the Stage you set.
slots.deliverable: A configured Opportunity Stage picklist with correct probabilities and forecast categories, a four-item Price Book, and five test Opportunities — one per stage — each with at least one product attached.

slots.practicalActivity: Build both custom objects from scratch in Setup — Installation Project and Service Contract — with every field from the lesson's tables, explicitly choosing Lookup (never Master-Detail) for every relationship field, and set tab visibility per profile as specified. Create one test Installation Project and one test Service Contract, each linked to a real Account from the previous slot.
slots.deliverable: Two working custom objects (Installation Project, Service Contract) with all fields built, correct Lookup relationships, per-profile tab visibility, and one linked test record for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the three Account page layouts (Restaurant, Key Account, Standard) with their Record Type/profile assignments, the Opportunity layout with the Path component plus Products and Installation Project related lists, both custom-object layouts, and the "Sales Workspace" Lightning App Page. Activate it as the default Opportunity record page for the Sales Rep and Sales Manager profiles, then log in as a test Sales Rep user and confirm the Path, related lists, and Account highlights panel all appear exactly as designed.
slots.deliverable: Three Account layouts, an Opportunity layout with Path, two custom-object layouts, and an activated "Sales Workspace" Lightning App Page, verified by viewing it as a test Sales Rep user.

slots.practicalActivity: Spend this hour populating Cascade's org with a richer, more realistic working set before automation gets layered on top: add 5 more test Accounts spread across the six Record Types (10 total), 2-3 Contacts per Account, and 10 Opportunities spread across all five stages with real products attached. This gives Chapter 3's automation and Chapter 4's reports something substantial to run against instead of a handful of placeholder records.
slots.deliverable: An org populated with at least 10 Accounts, 20+ Contacts, and 10 Opportunities with products attached, built using the exact fields and layouts from this chapter.

slots.practicalActivity: Re-open the Lesson 1 Definition of Done checklist and literally check off Requirements 1-3 (the lead-to-cash object model, the two custom objects, and the page layouts/Lightning App Page) against what you just built. Walk one full Lead by hand through conversion into a Closed-Won-bound Opportunity to confirm the entire Chapter 2 build genuinely holds together end to end before Chapter 3 adds security and automation on top of it.
slots.deliverable: The Definition of Done checklist with Requirements 1-3 checked off and dated, plus a written note confirming one Lead-to-Opportunity walkthrough succeeded end to end.

slots.practicalActivity: Build all seven roles under Setup → Users → Roles, with Nair, Wu, and Webb as separate branches reporting directly under VP of Sales. Clone and configure all four custom profiles plus the unmodified System Administrator profile, set Private OWD on all five core objects, and build the three owner-based sharing rules. Create one test user per custom profile and use Login As to verify Monica Reyes's role shows all six roles beneath her while Derek Oyelaran's shows only Baptiste and Kessler.
slots.deliverable: A fully implemented security model — seven roles, five profiles, five Private OWD settings, three sharing rules — verified with Login As against at least two test users.

slots.practicalActivity: Build both Flows from the lesson in your own org: the record-triggered "New Lead Auto-Assignment" Flow (sets Owner to Jordan Kessler and creates a same-day follow-up Task on every new Lead) and the "Log a Service Visit" Screen Flow (updates Install Status and appends dated notes to Equipment Summary), added as a Quick Action on the Installation Project layout. Create a test Lead to confirm the first Flow fires, then launch the Screen Flow from a test Installation Project and confirm both fields update.
slots.deliverable: Two working Flows in your org — a verified record-triggered Lead auto-assignment Flow and a verified Screen Flow launched via Quick Action — each tested against a real record.

slots.practicalActivity: Build all four validation rules: Loss Reason required on Closed Lost, Decision Maker confirmed before Negotiation/Review (including the new Primary_Contact__c lookup field it depends on), Target Install Date can't be in the past, and Annual Value must be positive. Test every rule with one failing save and one passing save, exactly as the lesson describes.
slots.deliverable: Four working validation rules across Opportunity, Installation Project, and Service Contract, each confirmed with one documented failing save and one passing save.

slots.practicalActivity: Add the Discount Percent and Approval Status fields to Opportunity, build the "Opportunity Discount Approval" approval process (entry criteria Discount_Percent__c > 15, Monica Reyes as a specified-user approver, Lock Record on submission), and add the Submit for Approval button to the Opportunity layout. Walk through the lesson's scenario on a test Opportunity: submit a 20% discount, then test both the approve path and the reject path.
slots.deliverable: A working approval process tested end to end on a test Opportunity through both the approve path and the reject path, with the resulting Task created on rejection.

slots.practicalActivity: Stress-test Chapter 3 before moving on: run the New Lead Auto-Assignment Flow against 5 new test Leads at once to confirm it behaves correctly for every one, deliberately trigger each of the four validation rules' failing case a second time to confirm the error messages are exactly right, and submit two more Opportunities through the approval process — one that should be blocked by the entry criteria and one that should trigger it — to confirm the threshold logic is exact.
slots.deliverable: A written test log covering 5 Lead-assignment runs, 4 repeated validation-rule failing-case checks, and 2 additional approval-process submissions (one below threshold, one above), with pass/fail noted for each.

slots.practicalActivity: Re-open the Definition of Done checklist and check off Requirements 4-7 (security model, record-triggered Flow, validation rules, approval process) against the real, tested build from this chapter. Draft the handoff document's Automation Inventory section, giving every Flow, validation rule, and the approval process the lesson's four-line treatment (name, type/trigger, what it does, why it exists), ready to carry into Chapter 4's documentation lesson.
slots.deliverable: The Definition of Done checklist with Requirements 4-7 checked off, plus a drafted Automation Inventory section listing every Flow, validation rule, and the approval process in the required four-line format.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the three report folders (Sales, Operations, Customer Success Reports) with the correct sharing, the three reports (Pipeline by Stage, Installation Backlog, Service Contract Renewals Coming Due) with the exact filters, groupings, and summaries specified, and the four-component Cascade Executive Dashboard running as Monica Reyes.
slots.deliverable: Three report folders with three working reports and one four-component Executive Dashboard, confirmed to run correctly as Monica Reyes.

slots.practicalActivity: Build the full realistic sample data set in the correct load order and with the correct tool for each object: 15 Accounts across all six Record Types (Import Wizard), 30 Contacts (Import Wizard), 20+ Opportunities across all five stages (Data Loader), 10 Installation Projects (Data Loader), and 7 Service Contracts with some intentionally "At Risk" (Data Loader), using Upsert to avoid duplicates. Confirm the previous slot's reports return real, varied numbers once this data is loaded.
slots.deliverable: A fully loaded sample data set — 15 Accounts, 30 Contacts, 20+ Opportunities, 10 Installation Projects, 7 Service Contracts — confirmed against the Chapter 4 reports returning real, varied numbers.

slots.practicalActivity: Run every test in the lesson's five sections against your own org — the six security-access tests (including the negative test), the three Flow tests, the four validation-rule failing/passing pairs, the three approval-process tests, and the report/dashboard checks — recording a pass/fail for each row, and fix anything that fails before moving on.
slots.deliverable: A completed test log with pass/fail recorded for all five sections (security, Flows, validation rules, approval process, reports/dashboard), with every failure resolved.

slots.practicalActivity: Write the full eight-section handoff document for your own build (Overview, Data Model, Security Model, Automation Inventory, Reports & Dashboards, Sample Data, Test Results, Known Limitations & Next Steps), pulling directly from the artifacts already created in Lessons 3, 4, 11-15, and 17, and writing an honest Known Limitations section (no Lightning Web Components, no outside-ERP integration, no Apex).
slots.deliverable: A complete eight-section written handoff document for the finished Cascade org, including an honest Known Limitations & Next Steps section.

slots.practicalActivity: Write and practice your own five-part walkthrough out loud, timed to 5-10 minutes: the scenario, the data model, the security model, one chosen automation story told as a before/after, and the reports plus one honest "what's next." Prepare written answers to the five likely interview questions in the lesson's table, and gather the data model diagram and role hierarchy diagram as visuals to bring to the walkthrough.
slots.deliverable: A timed, rehearsed five-part capstone walkthrough (5-10 minutes) plus written answers to the five likely interview questions and the two diagrams prepared as visual aids.

slots.practicalActivity: Write your own one-page retrospective: fill in "Built in Lesson ___" for all ten Definition of Done requirements against your real build, write three honest lessons learned (including the two fields that got added mid-build rather than pre-planned), and write one sentence on what you'd do differently on a second pass.
slots.deliverable: A completed one-page retrospective with the filled-in ten-row Definition of Done table, three lessons learned, and one improvement sentence.

slots.practicalActivity: Do a complete, cold run-through of the finished Cascade org as if demoing it for the first time to an interviewer: log in, open the Sales Workspace Lightning App Page on a real Opportunity, walk the Path, open the related Installation Project and Service Contract, then open the Executive Dashboard and confirm every component still renders correctly against the loaded sample data.
slots.deliverable: A screenshot set (or short recording) of the cold walkthrough showing the Sales Workspace, a linked Installation Project/Service Contract, and the correctly rendering Executive Dashboard.

slots.practicalActivity: Assemble the final capstone portfolio package: the finished handoff document, the retrospective, and the rehearsed five-part walkthrough script, all cross-checked against each other so the numbers and claims match exactly (the same report count, the same automation count, the same field names) before carrying this project into the next course's resume and interview work.
slots.deliverable: A finished, internally consistent capstone portfolio package — handoff document, retrospective, and walkthrough script — ready to be the primary project in the next course's resume and portfolio work.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: Can design and build, entirely from a business scenario, a complete declarative Salesforce implementation — a real data model, a least-privilege security model, Flow automation, validation rules, an approval process, and executive reporting — producing a tested, documented, portfolio-ready capstone to carry straight into the program's final job-search course.
